title: aleuritia gambeliana
intro: Aleuritia gambeliana, commonly known as the Desert Marigold, is a flowering plant species native to the southwestern United States and Mexico. The plant has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, with reported health benefits including the treatment of fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions. Its therapeutic actions are attributed to its ability to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and act as an antiseptic and antibacterial agent. The bioactive constituents of Aleuritia gambeliana include sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and alkaloids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and are still being studied for their potential health benefits.
